pr_title: Show warning when defaulting to Equity in SetBenchmark
pr_body:
#### Description
A warning message has been added in `SetBenchmark(string symbol)` when no existing security is found and the new benchmark security is being added with `SecurityType.Equity`.

#### Related Issue
Closes #2153

issue_context.title: SetBenchmark Silent Default to Equity
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Ideally the benchmark is resolved as BTCUSD not Equity.
```
SetBenchmark("BTCUSD");
AddCrypto("BTCUSD", Resolution.Minute);
```

#### Actual Behavior
BTCUSD added as Equity; and the AddCrypto line ignored. It was quite confusing as in this case the price was always $0 as there is no BTCUSD Equity. 

#### Potential Solution
Show a message about the Equity assumption? Scan market hours db to get security type? 

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue
comments:
I think the major issue here is providing an overload that doesn't require a security type, or rather a full symbol object. If required a full symbol object I think the code above would throw because BTCUSD wasn't added yet, but if the order was reversed then it would succeed since it now exists in the `SymbolCache`.

As always, wary of potential heuristics to resolve things that are more easily resolved by the user specifying the correct data.

EDIT: That being said, I think a message about the default behavior makes a lot of sense
The API will always require a level of design and heuristics to make it user-friendly. As the API designers, we walk that line of making it easy to use, flexible and requiring total specifications.

There may be a pending issue here with the ordering of the added security and resolving benchmark as there is code in place to select the right ticker: 
`var security = Securities.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Key.Value == symbol).Value;`
Issues with the call order of AddEquity and SetBenchmark should have been resolved in #2403

review_comments: We could add the information that there is a method overload that accepts the `SecurityType`: `SetBenchmark(SecurityType, string)`.
